title: Naming conventions
text: sample_map canonical, long-format sample table: one row per sample, number assays roles. New assays represented new rows, never new columns per-assay tables.

title: Naming conventions
text: assay free-form lowercase value, fixed enumeration. Pick stable label per assay reuse consistently. Common examples:

title: Naming conventions
text: myceliumr enforce specific sample ID formats, adopt consistent project-wide convention. Encoding assay role ID can aid readability: Tumor: {assay}_T{subject} (e.g., “wes_T101”, “wgs_T001”) Normal: {assay}_N{subject} (e.g., “wes_N101”, “wgs_N001”) Single-cell/RNA: {assay}_{subject}_{rep} (e.g., “scrna_101_1”, “bulk_rna_101_2”)

title: Naming conventions
text: Study objects: snake_case, descriptive (e.g., my_study, nf1_study) explicitly named study examples. Cohort objects: snake_case (e.g., cohort, nf1_cohort, study_cohort). Subject objects: Rarely used directly; accessed via cohort@subjects[[subject_id]]. AnalysisSpec objects: Use spec name primary identifier (stored registry name key). Data tables: snake_case _tbl suffix use descriptive names like subject_data, wes_samples.

title: Naming conventions
code: # Study study <- study_new(   study_id = "NF1_001",   title = "NF1 Rat Genomics Study" )  # Cohort cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = subject_data,   sample_map = sample_data,   study = study )  # Access subject subject <- cohort@subjects[["RAT_101"]]  # Access analysis result <- cohort@analyses[["my_analysis_name"]]

title: Naming conventions
text: Constructor functions: {noun}_new() (e.g., study_new(), cohort_new()) Validation functions: validate_{noun}() (e.g., validate_manifest(), validate_cohort()) Accessor/getter functions: get_{property}() simply reference property directly (e.g., cohort@subject_tbl) IO functions: read_{format}() write_{format}() (e.g., read_manifest_csv()) Helper functions: lowercase underscores (e.g., extract_pair_ids()) S7 methods: Dispatch class; function name describes operation (e.g., print() method Cohort)

title: Naming conventions
text: Class definitions: classes.R Constructors: constructors.R Validation: validate.R, validate_manifest.R IO (read/write): io.R Methods utilities: {feature}.R (e.g., analysis_registry.R, print.R)

title: Naming conventions
text: Raw data: Use consistent prefix descriptor (e.g., manifest_nf1_001.csv, cohort_pilot_data.rda) Intermediate data: {description}_{date}.rda {description}_{version}.fst Results: {analysis}_{date}_{version}.csv {analysis}_results.rda

title: Naming conventions

title: Naming conventions

title: Naming conventions

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: immutable S7 class defining analysis specifications Cohort. AnalysisSpec objects describe locate, read, interpret analysis output files templated paths standardized readers.

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
code: AnalysisSpec(   name = character(0),   assay = character(0),   level = character(0),   format = character(0),   description = NA_character_,   path_template = NA_character_,   root_key = NA_character_,   reader = character(0),   key_cols = character(0) )

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: name Character scalar unique analysis name (key registry). assay Character scalar assay type (e.g., "wes_somatic", "wes_germline", "snrna"). Required. level Character scalar data organization level. Must one : "subject", "pair", "cohort". Required. format Character scalar file format (e.g., "rds", "tsv", "txt"). Required. description Character scalar human-readable description analysis. Optional, defaults NA. path_template Character scalar templated path analysis output. Supports substitution tokens: {root}, {subject_id}, {tumor_id}, {normal_id}, {pair_id}. Optional, defaults NA. root_key Character scalar key cohort@paths list use {root} template value (e.g., "msi_root", "sig_root", "wes_root"). Optional, defaults NA. reader Character scalar function name read files matching spec (e.g., "read_msi_txt", "read.csv"). Must valid function name. Required. key_cols Character vector column names use keys loading analysis table. Determines rows indexed (e.g., c("subject_id") c("pair_id")). Required.

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: Use analysis_spec_new() construct AnalysisSpec objects immediate validation. AnalysisSpec objects typically registered Cohort via analysis_register(). Access properties via @ operator:
code: spec@name spec@assay spec@level spec@format spec@description spec@path_template spec@root_key spec@reader spec@key_cols

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: immutable S7 class managing cross-species cohort data. Cohorts combine validated subject-level metadata sample--assay mappings optional study context, file paths, analysis results. primary data container WES snRNA-seq analyses across rat, mouse, human studies.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
code: Cohort(   study = NULL,   subjects = list(),   subject_tbl = NULL,   sample_map = NULL,   paths = list(),   analyses = list(),   registry = list(),   cache = list() )

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: study Study object providing project-level context metadata, NULL applicable. Optional. subjects Named list Subject objects, automatically created subject_tbl rows cohort construction. Names subject IDs. Access individual subjects via: cohort@subjects[["RAT001"]]. subject_tbl tibble (data frame) containing subject-level metadata. Required columns: subject_id (character), species (rat/mouse/human). Optional columns: sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes. Validated validate_cohort(). sample_map canonical long-format tibble mapping subjects samples, one row per sample. Columns: subject_id, assay, sample_id, role. New assays represented new rows, never new columns. Validated validate_cohort(). paths Named list file paths data files results directories. Optional, defaults empty list. analyses Named list containing analysis results, intermediate tables, data objects later retrieval. Optional, defaults empty list. registry Named list AnalysisSpec objects defining registered analyses. Names correspond spec@name. Optional, defaults empty list. cache Named list optional memoization loaded analysis data. Optional, defaults empty list.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: Use cohort_new() construct Cohort objects comprehensive validation. Validation ensures: Required columns subject_tbl sample_map Valid species values (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity subject_tbl sample_map duplicate subject IDs Access properties via @ operator:
code: cohort@study         # Study object or NULL cohort@subjects      # Named list of Subject objects cohort@subjects[["RAT001"]]  # Individual Subject object cohort@subject_tbl   # Subject metadata table (for bulk operations) cohort@sample_map    # Sample mapping table cohort@paths         # File paths cohort@analyses      # Stored analysis results cohort@registry      # Named list of AnalysisSpec objects cohort@cache         # Memoization cache

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: immutable S7 class storing research project metadata cross-species genomics studies. Study objects provide high-level context configuration cohorts analyses involving rat, mouse, human subjects.

title: S7 Study class — Study
code: Study(   study_id = character(0),   title = character(0),   description = NA_character_,   hypotheses = character(0),   aims = character(0),   assays = character(0),   genome_builds = list(),   created_at = NULL,   tags = character(0) )

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: study_id Character scalar study identifier. Unique within project. title Character scalar study name/title. description Character scalar longer description study purpose, design, protocols. Can file path (ending .md, .txt, .rtf) read README content. Optional. hypotheses Character vector research hypotheses. Accepts multiple hypotheses. Optional. aims Character vector specific research aims. Accepts multiple aims. Optional. assays Character vector assay types used (e.g., "WES", "snRNA-seq"). Optional. genome_builds Named list mapping species genome build versions (e.g., list(rat = "rn7", mouse = "mm10", human = "hg38")). Supports rn6, rn7 rat; mm9, mm10, mm39 mouse; hg19, hg38 human. Optional. created_at POSIXct timestamp creation. Defaults current time. tags Character vector arbitrary tags categorization. Optional.

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: Use study_new() construct Study objects immediate validation. Access properties via @ operator:
code: study@study_id study@title study@description study@hypotheses study@aims study@assays study@genome_builds study@created_at study@tags

title: S7 Subject class — Subject
text: subject_id Character scalar unique subject identifier. species Character scalar species designation. Must one : "rat", "mouse", "human" (validated subject_new()). sex Character scalar biological sex (e.g., "M", "F"). Optional. strain Character scalar strain breed designation. Optional. genotype Character scalar genetic background modification (e.g., "WT", "KO"). Optional. cohort Character scalar cohort membership treatment group. Optional. timepoint Character scalar study timepoint collection date. Optional. notes Character scalar free-form annotations. Optional.

code: # Create and register specs study <- study_new(study_id = "STUDY001", title = "My Study") manifest <- data.frame(   subject_id = c("S1", "S1", "S2", "S2"),   species = c("rat", "rat", "rat", "rat"),   assay = c("wes", "wes", "wes", "wes"),   sample_id = c("WES_T1", "WES_N1", "WES_T2", "WES_N2"),   role = c("tumor", "normal", "tumor", "normal") ) parsed <- validate_manifest(manifest) cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = parsed$subject_tbl,   sample_map = parsed$sample_map,   study = study )  spec1 <- analysis_spec_new(   name = "somatic_vars",   assay = "wes_somatic",   level = "pair",   format = "tsv",   reader = "read_tsv",   key_cols = c("pair_id") )  spec2 <- analysis_spec_new(   name = "gene_expr",   assay = "snrna",   level = "subject",   format = "rds",   reader = "readRDS",   key_cols = c("subject_id") )  cohort <- analysis_register(cohort, spec1) cohort <- analysis_register(cohort, spec2) analysis_list(cohort) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   name         assay       level   format reader   root_key #>   <chr>        <chr>       <chr>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr>    #> 1 somatic_vars wes_somatic pair    tsv    read_tsv NA       #> 2 gene_expr    snrna       subject rds    readRDS  NA

Validate and create cohort manifest_split <- validate_manifest(manifest) cohort <- cohort_new(   study = study,   subject_tbl = manifest_split$subject_tbl,   sample_map = manifest_split$sample_map ) print(cohort) #> <myceliumr::Cohort> #>  @ study      : <myceliumr::Study> #>  .. @ study_id     : chr "STUDY001" #>  .. @ title        : chr "Cross-species study" #>  .. @ description  : chr NA #>  .. @ hypotheses   : chr(0)  #>  .. @ aims         : chr(0)  #>  .. @ assays       : chr [1:2] "WES" "snRNA-seq" #>  .. @ genome_builds: list() #>  .. @ created_at   : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-06-30 08:28:30" #>  .. @ tags         : chr(0)  #>  @ subjects   :List of 2 #>  .. $ RAT001: <myceliumr::Subject> #>  ..  ..@ subject_id: chr "RAT001" #>  ..  ..@ species   : chr "rat" #>  ..  ..@ sex       : chr "M" #>  ..  ..@ strain    : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ genotype  : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ cohort    : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ timepoint : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ notes     : chr NA #>  .. $ MOUSE1: <myceliumr::Subject> #>  ..  ..@ subject_id: chr "MOUSE1" #>  ..  ..@ species   : chr "mouse" #>  ..  ..@ sex       : chr "F" #>  ..  ..@ strain    : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ genotype  : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ cohort    : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ timepoint : chr NA #>  ..  ..@ notes     : chr NA #>  @ subject_tbl: tibble [2 × 3] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>  $ subject_id: chr [1:2] "RAT001" "MOUSE1" #>  $ species   : chr [1:2] "rat" "mouse" #>  $ sex       : chr [1:2] "M" "F" #>  @ sample_map : tibble [4 × 4] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>  $ subject_id: chr [1:4] "RAT001" "RAT001" "MOUSE1" "MOUSE1" #>  $ assay     : chr [1:4] "wes" "scrna" "wes" "atac" #>  $ sample_id : chr [1:4] "WES_T1" "RNA_1" "WES_T2" "ATAC_1" #>  $ role      : chr [1:4] "tumor" "tumor" "tumor" NA #>  @ paths      : list() #>  @ analyses   : list() #>  @ registry   : list() #>  @ cache      : list()  # Access individual Subject objects (automatically created) rat_subject <- cohort@subjects[["RAT001"]] print(rat_subject) #> <myceliumr::Subject> #>  @ subject_id: chr "RAT001" #>  @ species   : chr "rat" #>  @ sex       : chr "M" #>  @ strain    : chr NA #>  @ genotype  : chr NA #>  @ cohort    : chr NA #>  @ timepoint : chr NA #>  @ notes     : chr NA

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: Constructs Study object describe overall research project, including study metadata, research hypotheses aims, assay types, genome build information. Studies serve container cohorts provide context cross-species genomics analysis.

code: study_new(   study_id,   title,   description = NA_character_,   hypotheses = character(),   aims = character(),   assays = character(),   genome_builds = list(),   created_at = Sys.time(),   tags = character() )

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: study_id Character scalar providing unique identifier study. Must least 1 character long. title Character scalar study name/title. Must least 1 character long. description Character scalar optional longer description study purpose design. Can file path (ending .md, .txt, .rtf) read description field. Defaults NA. hypotheses Character vector research hypotheses. Accepts multiple hypotheses. Optional defaults empty vector. aims Character vector specific research aims. Accepts multiple aims. Optional defaults empty vector. assays Character vector assay types used study (e.g., "WES", "snRNA-seq"). Optional defaults empty vector. genome_builds Named list mapping species names genome build versions (e.g., list(rat = "rn7", mouse = "mm10")). Supports rn6, rn7 rat; mm9, mm10, mm39 mouse; hg19, hg38 human. Optional defaults empty list. created_at POSIXct timestamp study creation. Defaults current time. tags Character vector arbitrary tags categorization. Optional defaults empty vector.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Ensures Cohort object satisfies structural integrity requirements cross-species genomics analysis. Validates subject table, sample map, referential integrity . Intended internal validation step called automatically cohort_new().

code: validate_cohort(x)

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: x S7 object expected Cohort class instance.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Invisibly returns TRUE validation succeeds. Throws informative errors validation fails.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: VALIDATION CHECKS: x actually Cohort object subject_tbl sample_map data frames subject_tbl includes required columns: subject_id, species sample_map includes subject_id column subject_id species character vectors, non-empty duplicate subject_id values subject_tbl species values valid (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity: sample_map$subject_id values exist subject_tbl Validation performed automatically cohort_new(), can called directly debugging custom Cohort construction.

code: # Create valid cohort components subjects <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   species = "rat",   sex = "M" ) samples <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   assay = "wes",   sample_id = "WES_R001",   role = "tumor" ) cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = subjects,   sample_map = samples )  # Validation succeeds (called automatically above) validate_cohort(cohort)

what: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
text: Validates tidy, long-format manifest (one row per sample) structures subject metadata table canonical long-format sample map. design deliberately species- assay-agnostic: organism assay (WGS, WES, ATAC-seq, bulk RNA, single-cell, ...) represented values, never bespoke columns per-assay tables.

title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
code: validate_manifest(manifest, allow_duplicates = FALSE)

title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
text: manifest data.frame tibble long format, one row per sample. Required columns: subject_id (character; coerced): subject sample belongs . assay (character; coerced): assay type, e.g. "wgs", "wes", "atac", "bulk_rna", "scrna". sample_id (character; coerced): unique sample identifier. Optional sample-level column: role (character): role sample within assay, e.g. "tumor", "normal". Defaults NA absent. remaining columns (e.g. species, sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes) treated subject-level metadata must constant within subject_id. allow_duplicates Logical. FALSE (default), repeated (subject_id, assay, sample_id) combinations raise error. TRUE, duplicates kept.

title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
text: list three elements: subject_tbl: Tibble one row per subject_id containing subject-level metadata columns. sample_map: Canonical long-format tibble columns subject_id, assay, sample_id, role. completeness_tbl: Tibble one row per subject_id x assay summarising number samples (n_samples).

title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
text: Empty strings subject_id, assay, sample_id, role treated missing. Every sample row must carry non-missing subject_id, assay, sample_id. Per-assay wide views (e.g. tumor/normal pairs) part core contract; derive demand sample_map.

title: Validate and structure a long-format sample manifest — validate_manifest
code: manifest <- data.frame(   subject_id = c("RAT001", "RAT001", "MOUSE1", "HUM01"),   species = c("rat", "rat", "mouse", "human"),   assay = c("wes", "wes", "atac", "wgs"),   sample_id = c("WES_T1", "WES_N1", "ATAC_1", "WGS_T1"),   role = c("tumor", "normal", NA, "tumor"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  parsed <- validate_manifest(manifest) parsed$subject_tbl #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   subject_id species #>   <chr>      <chr>   #> 1 RAT001     rat     #> 2 MOUSE1     mouse   #> 3 HUM01      human   parsed$sample_map #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   subject_id assay sample_id role   #>   <chr>      <chr> <chr>     <chr>  #> 1 RAT001     wes   WES_T1    tumor  #> 2 RAT001     wes   WES_N1    normal #> 3 MOUSE1     atac  ATAC_1    NA     #> 4 HUM01      wgs   WGS_T1    tumor  parsed$completeness_tbl #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   subject_id assay n_samples #>   <chr>      <chr>     <int> #> 1 HUM01      wgs           1 #> 2 MOUSE1     atac          1 #> 3 RAT001     wes           2

title: myceliumr 0.3.0
text: Generic, species- assay-agnostic manifest layer (#7). manifest model longer hardcoded rat / WES / snRNA-seq. canonical representation tidy, long-format sample_map columns subject_id, assay, sample_id, role, assay free-form value (wgs, wes, atac, bulk_rna, scrna, …). New assays new rows, never new columns per-assay tables. validate_manifest() now takes single long-format manifest (required columns subject_id, assay, sample_id; optional role plus subject-level metadata) returns subject_tbl, sample_map, completeness_tbl. previous rat_id/wes_tumor_id/wes_normal_id/sn_id inputs dna_tbl/rna_tbl outputs removed. strict allow_rna_duplicates arguments replaced allow_duplicates. read_manifest_csv() now reads long-format CSV delegates validate_manifest(), restoring single source truth manifest parsing. returns three tables longer emits wes_pair_tbl. completeness_tbl now one row per subject_id x assay n_samples count, replacing WES-specific has_dna_* / n_rna_samples columns.
